findings.highlight: we should give our undivided attention to Kazusa's additional concert
findings.evidenceJa: 「今は、かずさを追加公演に専念させることが第一だと言うことで、彼女とも一致しました」
findings.explanation: Haruki and Miyoko agree that their first priority is keeping Kazusa focused on the additional concert. The English instead says they themselves should devote their undivided attention to it, shifting both the subject and the management plan.
findings.japanese:
「今は、かずさを追加公演に専念させることが
第一だと言うことで、彼女とも一致しました」
findings.todokanai: "I told her that we should give our undivided attention to Kazusa's additional concert, and she agreed."

findings.highlight: I'll give that girl a happy life no matter what it takes…
findings.evidenceJa: 二人じゃ、文殊の知恵は出ないかもしれないけれど、なんとしても、あいつが笑って暮らせる一生を…
findings.explanation: Haruki says that even if two heads may not produce wisdom, he and Youko must somehow find a whole life in which Kazusa can live smiling. The English turns that tentative collaborative search into Haruki's unilateral promise to give Kazusa a happy life.
findings.japanese:
二人じゃ、文殊の知恵は出ないかもしれないけれど、
なんとしても、あいつが笑って暮らせる一生を…
findings.todokanai: The two of us might not be able to come up with anything wise, but I'll give that girl a happy life no matter what it takes…

findings.highlight: "Decide after you've asked yourself if you value him or Kazusa more."
findings.evidenceJa: 「かずさとどっちを取るか考えた上で決めてください」
findings.explanation: Youko asks about men in general; the English's singular 'him' invents a specific current partner — Haruki's answer still communicates that she must choose Kazusa over romantic indulgence.
findings.japanese: 「かずさとどっちを取るか考えた上で決めてください」
findings.todokanai: "Decide after you've asked yourself if you value him or Kazusa more."

findings.highlight: I can't think of any other reason…
findings.evidenceJa: それが、熱気のこもった練習のせいなのか、治りきっていない患部が熱を持ってしまったのか、それ以外の理由なのかはわからなかったけど…
findings.explanation: Haruki cannot tell whether Kazusa's hot hands come from practice, inflammation, or some other reason—the final possibility quietly allows for emotional arousal. The English says he cannot think of any other reason, explicitly excluding the implication the source leaves open.
findings.japanese:
それが、熱気のこもった練習のせいなのか、
治りきっていない患部が熱を持ってしまったのか、
それ以外の理由なのかはわからなかったけど…
findings.todokanai: Perhaps it was due to her passionate practice up until now, or perhaps the result of an inflammation in her injured hands. I can't think of any other reason…

findings.highlight: I wanted to do it directly…
findings.evidenceJa: 「実は記事の最終チェック、事務所通してると時間かかるから、直接やってもらいたくてさ…」
findings.explanation: Haruki wants Kazusa to check the article directly because routing it through her office takes too long. The English says Haruki himself wants to do the check directly, reversing who is being asked to perform the work.
findings.japanese:
「実は記事の最終チェック、
事務所通してると時間かかるから、
直接やってもらいたくてさ…」
findings.todokanai: "The truth is, the final checking of the articles will take a while if I do it at the office, so I wanted to do it directly…"

findings.highlight: Kazusa just refuses to get a clue.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺がどれだけはぐらかしても、かずさは遠慮という名の拒絶をやめようとしなかった。
findings.explanation: Kazusa persists in a refusal she calls consideration or restraint: she knowingly tries to withdraw for Haruki's sake. 'Refuses to get a clue' instead portrays her as failing to understand his hints, reversing her awareness and motive.
findings.japanese:
俺がどれだけはぐらかしても、
かずさは遠慮という名の拒絶をやめようとしなかった。
findings.todokanai: No matter how much I try to change the topic, Kazusa just refuses to get a clue.

findings.highlight: The amount of damage she would receive really makes me not want to resort to this tactic.
findings.evidenceJa: 威力はともかく、あまりにダメージが大きいから、あまり使いたくはなかった作戦だったけど。
findings.explanation: Haruki's tactic is to move closer so Kazusa's refusal loses force, but doing so inflicts too much emotional damage on Haruki himself. The English assigns that damage to Kazusa, reversing the reason he hates using the tactic.
findings.japanese:
威力はともかく、あまりにダメージが大きいから、
あまり使いたくはなかった作戦だったけど。
findings.todokanai: Unfortunately, I wouldn't just be toning down the tension. The amount of damage she would receive really makes me not want to resort to this tactic.

findings.highlight: As long as you want me to, I'll do my very best for you, Kazusa…
findings.evidenceJa: 「かずさがそう言う限り、俺は俺の万全を尽くす。…今度こそ、お前の側にいる」
findings.explanation: Haruki means that as long as Kazusa keeps saying her concert failed because he did not come, he will do everything in his power and stay by her this time. The English changes that revealing dependence into a generic condition that she wants his help.
findings.japanese:
「かずさがそう言う限り、
俺は俺の万全を尽くす。
…今度こそ、お前の側にいる」
findings.todokanai: "As long as you want me to, I'll do my very best for you, Kazusa… This time, I'll be by your side."

findings.evidenceJa: 「そっか、ステーキか。うん、そんなの朝飯前だ。…いや、そんな時間に食うものじゃないけど」
findings.explanation: Haruki literalizes his own easy-task idiom and immediately corrects himself. Todokanai TL begins an English ‘piece of cake’ recreation but turns the payoff into unexplained dietary advice, so the self-correction does not land as intentional wordplay. An English recreation need not preserve the source's exact breakfast-hour mechanism; it does need a coherent literalized-idiom punchline.
findings.japanese:
「そっか、ステーキか。
うん、そんなの朝飯前だ。
…いや、そんな時間に食うものじゃないけど」
findings.todokanai: "I see, you want steak. Yes, making that should be a piece of cake… no, you should probably avoid cake."
